roleTitle: Software Quality Engineer, Customer Ticketing System
jobDescription: The customer ticketing system vendor ships its support product to cloud customers weekly. The Software Quality Engineer owns quality for the ticket-routing service end-to-end: sets the test strategy, decides release scope with the development lead, holds the go/no-go for each weekly release, and is accountable for escaped defects to the VP of engineering.
requirements: Owns quality for the ticket-routing service end-to-end and holds the go/no-go for each weekly release.
Maintains the service's automated test suites and the release-gate checks in the pipeline.
Analyses escaped defects and records root causes and prevention actions.
Coordinates release scope with the development lead and support operations and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each release.

evidence.text: Maintained the ticket-routing service's automated test suites (unit, contract and load) and the release-gate checks in the pipeline, adding a routing-rule regression pack after two escaped defects in rule evaluation.
Analysed escaped defects each fortnight, recording root causes and prevention actions in the quality log and presenting them at the engineering review.

Coordinated release scope with the development lead and support operations in the weekly release meeting; the development lead set the scope and the release manager held the go/no-go for each weekly release.
Wrote the release quality notes for each release, listing known limitations (load tests did not cover the enterprise tier's rule volumes) and the hand-over items for support operations.
Responsibilities included test-suite maintenance, release-gate checks, escaped-defect analysis and release quality notes for the ticket-routing service over about two years.
Work sample: the release-gate check configuration and the quality log for one quarter, with the pipeline run identifiers as a verification trail.

Hiring manager pre-read: the VP of engineering wants a quality engineer who has personally held the weekly go/no-go; in the screen the candidate said the release manager 'basically rubber-stamped what I recommended'.
Reference call with the former development lead: described the candidate as 'the conscience of the release process' and 'the one who really ran quality for routing'; confirmed employment dates.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the ticket-routing service's automated test suites and release-gate checks and added a routing-rule regression pack.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the gate configuration document the suites and checks.

propositions.text: The candidate analysed escaped defects fortnightly and recorded root causes and prevention actions in the quality log.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the quality log document the analysis.

propositions.text: The candidate owned quality for the ticket-routing service end-to-end and held the weekly go/no-go.
propositions.rationale: The resume assigns scope to the development lead and the go/no-go to the release manager; 'rubber-stamped' and 'really ran quality' describe influence and opinion, not authority held.

gold.expectedGap: The materials show suites, gate checks and defect analysis; they do not show the candidate holding the go/no-go or setting release scope.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the boundary the resume states: scope by the development lead, go/no-go by the release manager; the candidate recommended.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate ever held the go/no-go himself and for which releases, and who could overrule his recommendation.
